chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He can stipulate upon her whatever he so desires from the days (term).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on stipulating a time period in a marriage contract according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This brief hadith from al-Kafi underscores the permissibility of stipulating a fixed duration in marriage contracts, a key feature of Shia jurisprudence often associated with 'Mut'ah marriage.' It reflects the scholarly view that the time limit is a flexible condition agreed upon by the spouses, allowing for adaptability in marital arrangements. The narration highlights the legal autonomy granted to parties in defining the temporal scope of their union.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboun, from Ali Bin Raib, from Umar Bin Hanzala, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘He can stipulate upon her whatever he so desires to, from the days (term)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
He can arrange for a mutual agreement with her for any number of days they want.’”
